glosses: A short jump.

examples.text: The frog crossed the brook in three or four hops.

glosses: A jump on one leg.
A short journey, especially in the case of air travel, one that takes place on a private plane.

examples.text: My fellow passengers are a mixture of people returning from a day out in the capital, locals doing short hops, and a few (like me) heading farther afield.

glosses: A brief period of development or progress.

examples.text: For popular radio stars in New York and Los Angeles, it was a short hop to network television.

glosses: A bounce, especially from the ground, of a thrown or batted ball.
A dance; a gathering for the purpose of dancing.

examples.text:

One singing-room we had closed, and so damaged a "twopenny hop" that it could not have survived another season had our own prosperity continued unchecked.

glosses: The sending of a data packet from one host to an adjacent host as part of its overall journey.
To jump a short distance.

examples.text: When it had advanced from the wood, it hopped much after the fashion of a kangaroo, using its hind feet and tail to propel it, and when it stood erect, it sat upon its tail.

glosses: To jump on one foot.
To be in state of energetic activity.

examples.text: Sorry, can't chat. Got to hop.
The sudden rush of customers had everyone in the shop hopping.

glosses: To suddenly take a mode of transportation that one does not drive oneself, often surreptitiously.

examples.text: I hopped a plane over here as soon as I heard the news.
He was trying to hop a ride in an empty trailer headed north.
He hopped a train to California.

glosses: To jump onto, or over

examples.text: They hop the curb and cut their engines.

As the 1857 to Manchester Piccadilly rolls in, I scan the windows and realise there are plenty of spare seats, so I hop aboard. The train is a '221'+'220' combo to allow for social distancing - a luxury on an XC train as normally you're playing sardines, so I make the most of it.

glosses: To move frequently from one place or situation to another similar one.

examples.text: We were party-hopping all weekend.
bar-hopping
We had to island-hop on the weekly seaplane to get to his hideaway.

glosses: To go in a quick or sudden manner.

examples.text: We hopped on the freeway heading to LA and I looked over at the dashboard and saw the needle back on “E” and I told the guy, “Hey! You going to make it with the gas you got?"

Spangler hopped up from the control panel and stretched, pressing his hands to his lower back.
